sources.used_for: Rounded Say span, wrist span, 4-inch shoulder span, 8-inch body width, 55-inch overall length; paragraph wing area and parallel inner/elliptical outer planform. Derived AR from the rounded span.
Two wing regions, conventional tail, fin and rudder as an educational mechanical interpretation.

assumptions: 6 kg mass, 400 W motor and 65% propulsive efficiency are benchmark assumptions, not Stanley's measured values.
Cycle-averaged lift/drag/thrust; 2 Hz visual flapping, 0.45 rad inner amplitude and phase-shifted outer articulation are new assumptions.
A parallel central panel and sampled elliptical outer panel are a geometric idealization; thickness, tail shape and landing gear are illustrative.
excluded_fields: The printed 3.135 ft wing length conflicts with the scaled value and is excluded.
The 7.83 table and crossed-out 14% comparison are unavailable/uncertain.
Biological stroke-angle axes and vortex-lift landing claims on page 14 are not numeric constraints.
limitations: An educational point-mass demonstrator, not a validated aircraft or prediction of real flight.
No aeroelasticity, structural loads, wake history, measured polar, wing-inertia energy or actual motor mechanism.
Body geometry and controls are assumed; no recovered engineering design is claimed.
